edges.label: restore the previous value · show why

cards.title: The outbox, five steps
items: 1 · write the optimistic row and the queued mutation in one transaction; 2 · send with an idempotency key; 3 · on success write the server's answer and settle the row; 4 · on failure restore the previous value and show why; 5 · drain on reconnect, foreground and a background task
without steps 1 and 4 it is data loss with a spinner — the optimistic row is the visible promise, the rollback is the promise kept
the outbox is persisted and survives app restarts; a queued mutation that never drains is a visible defect, not a silent one

cards.title: No broker, no server queue
items: the queue is local state and the drain is a foreground or background task — there is no message bus, no server-side topic and no polling daemon to run
the write path is the ViewModel and the SDK; the View never calls the network, and a mutation never skips the queue to be fast
TanStack Query carries the server state — cache keys, retries, dedupe and background refresh — and the query cache is the last good data

cards.title: The server wins a conflict
items: the local pending change is rejected visibly, never silently dropped; a rejected mutation leaves the screen showing why
the idempotency key makes a retry safe — a drained mutation sent twice is one mutation at the server
invalidate by prefix after a mutation, never refetch the world; pagination is cursor-based so a list grows without loading everything
